description:
FILED s514f (Opus, 2026-10-10) while writing the #3143 guard rows in Pl/t/imported-term-01.t.

The gate's shared transpile server (PCL_XSERVER, set by Pl/t/PCLCore.pm and inherited by everything a test file spawns) DROPS the `-I` list of a MODULE transpile.  The runtime spawns a module unit's transpile as `perl -I<program @INC...> pl2cl --module --deps F -- Module.pm` (p-transpile-file, %p-transpile-inc-args); pl2cl's client block forwards flags + environment + cwd to the server, but NOT perl's own switches (pl2cl's header comment says so: "a caller that runs `perl -I<dir> pl2cl` would get a server without that -I ... No such caller sets PCL_XSERVER today" -- the runtime IS such a caller, under every Pl/t file).

Effect: inside a Pl/t row, a module UNIT that `use`s a sibling module reachable only through the program's `use lib` dir gets NO prototype facts for it -- the sibling's import is an unknown word, so `f @l, 5` with an imported `f($$)` passes 4 args (perl: 2) and the detector announces.  Outside the gate (runpcl, pcl, the sweep) the -I reaches the child and it is right.

Reproducer (scratch/s514f/pr/rep.pl in the s514f worktree): a tempdir lib with T3143/PA.pm (`sub f($$)`, exported) and T3143/User.pm (`package T3143::User; use T3143::PA qw(f); sub u { my @l=(1,2,3); f @l, 5 }`), program `use lib DIR; use T3143::User; print T3143::User::u()` -- `f(2)` with PCL_XSERVER unset, `f(4)` + a detector line with PCL_XSERVER=<socket>.

So the gate silently under-tests every module-unit path that depends on a `use lib` dir.  Fix direction: carry the child's @INC (or its -I list) in the server request and have the server answer with that inc_paths (its L1 prototype memo is keyed by module NAME, which then also needs the inc list in its key), or have the client DECLINE when perl was started with -I (detectable by comparing @INC against PERL5LIB + the compiled-in default).  The #3143 row works around it with `local $ENV{PCL_XSERVER} = ''`.
subject: The gate's transpile server (PCL_XSERVER) drops the -I list of a MODULE transpile the runtime spawns -- module units lose use-lib siblings' prototypes inside Pl/t only
